rules.title: A label in the lyric text
rules.message: Review this bracketed label for Musixmatch.
rules.explanation: Musixmatch keeps section and performer tags outside lyric text. Confirm this is metadata; bracketed vocals and uncertain words must remain until their meaning is known. Switching retains recognized Genius metadata separately.

rules.title: A repeat count without the lyrics
rules.message: Write the repeated lyrics instead of this placeholder.
rules.explanation: The source asks transcribers to include repeated words. No automatic expansion is offered because the intended earlier section may be ambiguous.

rules.title: A censor mask without audible letters
rules.message: Confirm the audible part of this censored word.
rules.explanation: Musixmatch transcribes audible expletives and represents an audio-censored cutoff with a hyphen. Stars do not establish which letters were heard; listen before replacing them.

rules.title: An unconfirmed sound description
rules.message: Confirm whether this is a sound description.
rules.explanation: Musixmatch excludes descriptions of production sounds but retains sung vocalizations. Asterisks alone do not establish that distinction; keep the text until its role is confirmed.

rules.title: A word still needing transcription
rules.message: This word still needs transcription.
rules.explanation: The English Musixmatch FAQ rejects question-mark replacement tokens. Keep this uncertainty visible until listening or research establishes the word; deleting the token or inventing lyrics would lose information.

rules.title: More than ten lines in a lyric block
rules.message: This lyric block has more than ten lines.
rules.explanation: Musixmatch limits formatted sections to ten physical lyric lines. Choose a break that follows the music and meaning; soft wraps are not extra lines, and a layout break does not establish a new musical tag.
rules.flaggedExample:
Here we sing
Here we stand
Here we turn
Here we rest
Here we dream
Here we wait
Here we dance
Here we stay
Here we walk
Here we rise
Here we return
rules.acceptedExample:
Here we sing
Here we stand

Here we turn

rules.title: A lowercase line beginning
rules.message: Review the lowercase line beginning.
rules.explanation: Musixmatch capitalizes lyric line beginnings. Preserve established name casing and review mixed-language context before changing it.

rules.title: A lowercase sentence beginning
rules.message: Review the lowercase sentence beginning.
rules.explanation: Capitalize the start after a question or exclamation when it begins a new sentence. Names and quoted fragments require context.

rules.title: Expressive capitals needing review
rules.message: Review this line’s expressive capitalization.
rules.explanation: Musixmatch does not use all-caps for shouting or arbitrary title case. Names, acronyms, German nouns and embedded languages require context; no automatic lowercasing is offered.

rules.title: Capitalized backing vocals
rules.message: Review capitalization in these backing vocals.
rules.explanation: Musixmatch normally uses grammatical case inside backing-vocal parentheses. A name, a new sentence, or another vocal role can justify the capital; do not lowercase all parenthetical lyrics.

rules.title: Terminal punctuation needing review
rules.message: Review this terminal period.
rules.explanation: Musixmatch excludes commas and non-acronym periods at lyric line endings. Acronyms retain their own punctuation; review names and abbreviations before removal.

rules.title: Repeated expressive punctuation
rules.message: Review repeated question or exclamation marks.
rules.explanation: Musixmatch permits these marks with restraint. Keep the mark needed by grammar or delivery; expressive intent and title punctuation require review.

rules.title: An unconfirmed interruption
rules.message: Confirm the reason for this line-ending interruption.
rules.explanation: Musixmatch uses a hyphen for an unfinished word and an ellipsis for an unfinished sentence or fade-out. A musical pause alone does not establish either; a Genius dropped-word dash cannot be rewritten from shape alone.

rules.title: A number without established context
rules.message: Confirm this number’s meaning before converting it.
rules.explanation: Musixmatch generally spells quantities through ten and uses digits above ten, with separate rules for dates, phones, decades, names, fixed expressions and times. Exact times and o’clock differ. A value alone does not prove its role or pronunciation; no numeric rewrite is offered.

rules.title: A contextual slang spelling
rules.message: Review this standardized slang spelling.
rules.explanation: Musixmatch lists a finite set of standardized forms. Apply this form only if the sung word has that meaning; names, dialect and letter-by-letter delivery must remain as heard.

rules.title: A quotation with unconfirmed meaning
rules.message: Confirm this quotation’s role and punctuation.
rules.explanation: Spanish direct speech uses a colon, a space and an opening quotation mark, except when the colon would end a line. Indirect speech and hypothetical words differ; quoted artist, song or album names are not necessarily speech.

rules.title: An instrumental interval needing review
rules.message: Confirm this instrumental interval.
rules.explanation: Musixmatch uses this marker only for more than fifteen consecutive seconds without qualifying lyrics between separately tagged sections, never inside a section or at a track edge. Whole-track instrumental status is separate. Text or two lyric-start times cannot prove the interval.

rules.title: Spanish backing-vocal placement
rules.message: Review the placement of these secondary vocals.
rules.explanation: Spanish guidance avoids initial or whole-line backing parentheses and punctuation immediately before them. Confirm lead, background, audience and overlapping roles before moving or unwrapping text; the change can affect timing.

rules.title: A possible Spanish acronym
rules.message: Confirm whether these letters form an acronym.
rules.explanation: The Spanish FAQ writes acronyms in capitals without separating dots or spaces. Sung individual letters, abbreviations and names are different cases; their role cannot be inferred from punctuation alone.

rules.title: A source-specific Spanish accent
rules.message: Review this Spanish accent convention.
rules.explanation: The Musixmatch Spanish FAQ uses these specified words without a written accent. Check quoted names or embedded-language text before changing the form; this is not a general accent-removal rule.

rules.title: A long Spanish lyric line
rules.message: Review this line against the Spanish character limit.
rules.explanation: The Spanish FAQ limits lines to 70 characters but does not define the Unicode counting unit. This line has 80 UTF-16 units and 80 Unicode code points. Review musical phrasing and the count; do not split automatically at an arbitrary position.
rules.flaggedExample: Volvemos al camino donde cantan los recuerdos y nos esperan las voces del viento
rules.acceptedExample:
Volvemos al camino
Donde nos esperan las voces del viento

rules.title: Restricted French punctuation
rules.message: Review this mark under the French guideline.
rules.explanation: French Musixmatch guidance excludes exclamation marks, colons and semicolons, except punctuation that belongs to a sung song title. Preserve title punctuation; a text-only check cannot establish that exception.

rules.title: A space before a French question mark
rules.message: Remove the space before this question mark.
rules.explanation: The French Musixmatch article specifically places a question mark without a preceding space. This lyric convention differs from some ordinary French publishing typography.

rules.title: An apostrophe in the French y a form
rules.message: Review the apostrophe in y a.
rules.explanation: The French Musixmatch FAQ writes this spoken form as y a, without an apostrophe. Preserve unrelated quoted names or embedded languages.

rules.title: A Japanese punctuation width mismatch
rules.message: Match this punctuation to the preceding character width.
rules.explanation: The Japanese Musixmatch FAQ uses fullwidth question and exclamation marks after fullwidth characters and ASCII marks after halfwidth characters. Only this mark changes; lyric scripts and other character forms stay exact.

rules.title: Language-specific evidence still missing
rules.message: Review the language-specific policy coverage.
rules.explanation: No reviewed Arabic-specific Musixmatch source establishes numeric morphology, digit-set conversion, dialect normalization, or orthographic exceptions. General Musixmatch checks run where their scope applies; no English spelling, number conversion or transliteration fallback is used. This is an evidence gap, not a claim that the lyrics are wrong.

guidance.title: Contribution rules apply across community, artist, representative, publisher and distributor accounts
guidance.statement: Contribution rules apply across community, artist, representative, publisher and distributor accounts; tools/submission paths differ.
guidance.note: Workflow: distinguish guideline support from having a native submission integration.

guidance.title: Listen to the whole recording and produce the transcription yourself
guidance.statement: Listen to the whole recording and produce the transcription yourself; do not copy another source's transcription.
guidance.note: Workflow: conversion cannot certify authorship, listening or provenance.

guidance.title: Include the complete vocal material, including producer tags, backing vocals and live performer/audience interjections
guidance.statement: Include the complete vocal material, including producer tags, backing vocals and live performer/audience interjections.
guidance.note: Review: retain vocals; switching cannot choose the recording or prove completeness.

guidance.title: Write every actual repetition
guidance.statement: Write every actual repetition; do not substitute a multiplier for repeated lyrics.
guidance.note: Check: shared placeholder finding is possible. Expansion requires known scope, count and wording.

guidance.title: Preserve audible expletives
guidance.statement: Preserve audible expletives; represent an actual censored cutoff with a hyphen rather than asterisks.
guidance.note: Review: mask→prefix is information loss in reverse; a hyphen alone does not establish censoring.

guidance.title: Exclude section and artist labels from the transcription text
guidance.statement: Exclude section and artist labels from the transcription text.
guidance.note: Convert/retain recognized syntax as metadata; ambiguous brackets stay visible.

guidance.title: Exclude production-sound effects and descriptions
guidance.statement: Exclude production-sound effects and descriptions.
guidance.note: Convert/retain only when the item is known to be a description, not sung text or a censor mask.

guidance.title: Include significant filler/vocalization, with moderation rather than exhaustive prolonged vowel strings
guidance.statement: Include significant filler/vocalization, with moderation rather than exhaustive prolonged vowel strings.
guidance.note: Review: stylistic significance and echo origin require listening. Never delete repeated vowels automatically.

guidance.title: Generally use original scripts
guidance.statement: Generally use original scripts; consult the linked romanization guidance for details.
guidance.note: Retain original script; no automatic transliteration. See official supplemental sources below.

guidance.title: Potential hate speech, slurs/dehumanization, incitement, discriminatory conspiracy claims and extremist material require accuracy review with other contributors, including a Specialist
guidance.statement: Potential hate speech, slurs/dehumanization, incitement, discriminatory conspiracy claims and extremist material require accuracy review with other contributors, including a Specialist; without agreement, leave the task; an internal ticket path is provided.
guidance.note: Workflow: document MXM's contribution process, without generating censorship rewrites, asserting verification, or contacting anybody automatically.

guidance.title: Divide lyrics according to musical structure
guidance.statement: Divide lyrics according to musical structure; a formatted section has at most ten lines.
guidance.note: Check/review: count actual lyric lines, not soft wraps; splitting requires an appropriate boundary.

guidance.title: Capitalize line beginnings and proper nouns
guidance.statement: Capitalize line beginnings and proper nouns.
guidance.note: Check only cased scripts and reviewed contexts; proper-name inference is not automatic proof.

guidance.title: Capitalize the following start after a question/exclamation
guidance.statement: Capitalize the following start after a question/exclamation.
guidance.note: Check/review sentence starts under the language policy.

guidance.title: Do not use arbitrary title capitals or uppercase to depict shouting
guidance.statement: Do not use arbitrary title capitals or uppercase to depict shouting.
guidance.note: Check/review; preserve acronyms and established name casing.

guidance.title: Parenthetical backing vocals take capitals when grammar calls for them
guidance.statement: Parenthetical backing vocals take capitals when grammar calls for them.
guidance.note: Review contextual changes; do not globally lowercase parenthetical beginnings.

guidance.title: Ordinary numbers above ten use digits
guidance.statement: Ordinary numbers above ten use digits; ten and below use words.
guidance.note: Convert only recognized quantities under a reviewed language-specific numeric policy.

guidance.title: Phone numbers, dates and decades use numerical forms
guidance.statement: Phone numbers, dates and decades use numerical forms.
guidance.note: Preserve identifier strings/leading zeros; classify dates separately from counts.

guidance.title: Exact times use digits, but an o'clock time spells its number
guidance.statement: Exact times use digits, but an o'clock time spells its number.
guidance.note: Convert only an established time expression; retain its source form.

guidance.title: No terminal comma or non-acronym period
guidance.statement: No terminal comma or non-acronym period.
guidance.note: Check with MXM provenance and an acronym-aware predicate; resolve language-specific punctuation qualifications.

guidance.title: Question and exclamation marks are permitted with restraint
guidance.statement: Question and exclamation marks are permitted with restraint.
guidance.note: Check/review; French restrictions below prevent universal reuse.

guidance.title: End hyphens/ellipses indicate interruption or fade-out
guidance.statement: End hyphens/ellipses indicate interruption or fade-out.
guidance.note: Review the semantic kind before transforming punctuation; no global dash replacement.

guidance.title: Use the supplied standardized slang forms, with meaning-sensitive distinctions
guidance.statement: Use the supplied standardized slang forms, with meaning-sensitive distinctions.
guidance.note: Share only evidenced overlaps; a Genius dictionary is not an MXM dictionary.

guidance.title: Introduce direct speech with a comma, enclose it in quotation marks and capitalize its beginning
guidance.statement: Introduce direct speech with a comma, enclose it in quotation marks and capitalize its beginning.
guidance.note: Review speech recognition. Curly glyphs in MXM examples do not by themselves mandate curly quotes. Spanish has a specific colon instruction.

guidance.title: Correct transcription errors while syncing
guidance.statement: Correct transcription errors while syncing; saving endorses the contribution as a whole.
guidance.note: Workflow: successful formatting/timing checks cannot certify the whole contribution.

guidance.title: Align each line with the onset of its first sung character, without an artificial breathing lead-in
guidance.statement: Align each line with the onset of its first sung character, without an artificial breathing lead-in.
guidance.note: Preserve authored timing; do not shift every timestamp or claim audio alignment from text.

guidance.title: Review each line and refine its timing
guidance.statement: Review each line and refine its timing; the native tools provide per-line adjustments and restart.
guidance.note: Workflow: our existing controls may support editing, but copied text does not transfer sync automatically.

guidance.title: Listen to full lines and work carefully
guidance.statement: Listen to full lines and work carefully; the source illustrates that syncing should take at least the recording's duration.
guidance.note: Human/audio review, not a deterministic elapsed-time validator or a delay imposed by the editor.

guidance.title: A distinct opening passage, at the beginning
guidance.statement: A distinct opening passage, at the beginning.
guidance.note: Convert a known type; do not infer it merely because a paragraph is first.

guidance.title: Narrative passage whose music commonly returns with changed words
guidance.statement: Narrative passage whose music commonly returns with changed words.
guidance.note: Preserve known structure; differing text alone does not prove a Verse.

guidance.title: A connecting passage preparing a chorus, commonly after a verse
guidance.statement: A connecting passage preparing a chorus, commonly after a verse.
guidance.note: Convert known type; do not invent it from position.

guidance.title: A prominent memorable passage, often repeating unchanged
guidance.statement: A prominent memorable passage, often repeating unchanged.
guidance.note: Matching repeated text does not alone establish the type.

guidance.title: A catchy, often more repetitive and less melodic/lyrical passage, distinguished from Chorus
guidance.statement: A catchy, often more repetitive and less melodic/lyrical passage, distinguished from Chorus.
guidance.note: Preserve distinction; explicit target decision when correspondence is not established.

guidance.title: A contrasting passage, commonly later in the song and between chorus repetitions
guidance.statement: A contrasting passage, commonly later in the song and between chorus repetitions.
guidance.note: The source's approximate position is descriptive, not a percentage-based detector.

guidance.title: A concluding passage at the end, possibly distinguished by music despite repeated words
guidance.statement: A concluding passage at the end, possibly distinguished by music despite repeated words.
guidance.note: Type is not derivable from repeated wording or final position alone.

guidance.title: Do not force every available type into a song
guidance.statement: Do not force every available type into a song; genre/tradition can change interpretation.
guidance.note: Seven described tags do not justify lossy collapse of all other source concepts.

guidance.title: Listen to the full recording and assign a structure tag to each section
guidance.statement: Listen to the full recording and assign a structure tag to each section.
guidance.note: Metadata workflow; no implication that tag labels are copied lyric text.

guidance.title: For an interior stretch exceeding 15 consecutive seconds without lyrics, type and sync an `#INSTRUMENTAL` lyric line
guidance.statement: For an interior stretch exceeding 15 consecutive seconds without lyrics, type and sync an `#INSTRUMENTAL` lyric line.
guidance.note: Require known interval boundaries and no qualifying lyrical content; vocalization/joik classification requires review. Two lyric-start anchors do not establish duration.

guidance.title: Put that marker between separately tagged sections, never inside one or at the song's beginning/end
guidance.statement: Put that marker between separately tagged sections, never inside one or at the song's beginning/end.
guidance.note: Check known placement; do not convert an entire instrumental song to this marker.

guidance.title: Put a blank line after the instrumental marker
guidance.statement: Put a blank line after the instrumental marker.
guidance.note: Source conflict for Japanese; no automatic shared spacing rule.

guidance.title: Seek community help for uncertain structure instead of forcing a type
guidance.statement: Seek community help for uncertain structure instead of forcing a type.
guidance.note: Review with an explicit unknown/unresolved state; no automatic outreach.

guidance.title: The described feature is desktop-only
guidance.statement: The described feature is desktop-only.
guidance.note: This limits native handoff claims, not LyricLint's ability to retain local metadata on a phone.

guidance.title: Finish required structure tags and other contribution work before performer tagging
guidance.statement: Finish required structure tags and other contribution work before performer tagging.
guidance.note: Metadata workflow; explicit sections are a prerequisite for native section tagging.

guidance.title: Listen to each complete section before assigning its performers
guidance.statement: Listen to each complete section before assigning its performers.
guidance.note: Review identity; roster presence is not proof of who sang.

guidance.title: A single performer can be assigned to an entire section
guidance.statement: A single performer can be assigned to an entire section.
guidance.note: Convert known section assignment into metadata.

guidance.title: For multiple performers, select their particular lyric ranges and tag each
guidance.statement: For multiple performers, select their particular lyric ranges and tag each.
guidance.note: Retain full range/group identity; no evidence for a four-style MXM limit.

guidance.title: Tag individual people rather than bands, using their commonly known stage names
guidance.statement: Tag individual people rather than bands, using their commonly known stage names.
guidance.note: Do not expand a band into guessed members, rename people, or infer identities.

guidance.title: Fanchant category covers crowd/uncredited-ensemble vocals
guidance.statement: Fanchant category covers crowd/uncredited-ensemble vocals; the prose names K-pop, while its linked example is outside K-pop.
guidance.note: Preserve category as explicit fact; genre scope needs clarification before a restrictive rule.

guidance.title: Voice-over category covers primary lyrics from an uncredited, unrecognized human voice
guidance.statement: Voice-over category covers primary lyrics from an uncredited, unrecognized human voice.
guidance.note: Review vocal role; unknown identity alone does not select this category.

guidance.title: Backing-vocalist category covers backing vocals without a credited/recognized performer
guidance.statement: Backing-vocalist category covers backing vocals without a credited/recognized performer.
guidance.note: Review role separately from performer identity.

guidance.title: Robotic-vocal category covers voices edited beyond recognition as human
guidance.statement: Robotic-vocal category covers voices edited beyond recognition as human.
guidance.note: No automatic AI↔robotic equivalence.

guidance.title: Ask the community about difficult cases
guidance.statement: Ask the community about difficult cases.
guidance.note: Workflow only; no external messages from the engine.

guidance.title: The described translation feature is desktop-only
guidance.statement: The described translation feature is desktop-only.
guidance.note: Native workflow limitation; local preservation is a separate capability.

guidance.title: Translate the existing formatted lines individually
guidance.statement: Translate the existing formatted lines individually; do not combine several source lines into one translation line.
guidance.note: Preserve known alignment metadata; no automatic translation. Japanese has a meaning-distribution qualification.

guidance.title: Prefer verified, locked source lyrics to reduce later translation loss
guidance.statement: Prefer verified, locked source lyrics to reduce later translation loss.
guidance.note: Recommendation, not a text-validation error or a claim LyricLint can verify the lock.

guidance.title: Transcription and formatting rules also apply to translations
guidance.statement: Transcription and formatting rules also apply to translations.
guidance.note: Track translation status explicitly; do not infer it from script/header vocabulary.

guidance.title: Preserve the source line's tone
guidance.statement: Preserve the source line's tone.
guidance.note: Human linguistic review.

guidance.title: Retain words/names that cannot sensibly be translated
guidance.statement: Retain words/names that cannot sensibly be translated.
guidance.note: No automatic proper-name translation or normalization.

guidance.title: Convey the intended message idiomatically instead of mechanically translating each word
guidance.statement: Convey the intended message idiomatically instead of mechanically translating each word.
guidance.note: Outside deterministic format conversion.

guidance.title: Seek help/research instead of leaving blanks or question-mark replacement tokens for undeciphered words
guidance.statement: Seek help/research instead of leaving blanks or question-mark replacement tokens for undeciphered words.
guidance.note: Direct conflict with Genius `[?]` for English. Keep the uncertainty visible as unresolved work; neither delete the token nor invent a word.

guidance.title: Ask for confirmation of unlisted abbreviated forms
guidance.statement: Ask for confirmation of unlisted abbreviated forms.
guidance.note: A deterministic engine can report missing coverage, not invent an approved spelling or contact a contributor.

guidance.title: Secondary vocals use parentheses and generally lowercase beginnings unless grammar or sentence-ending punctuation calls for capitals
guidance.statement: Secondary vocals use parentheses and generally lowercase beginnings unless grammar or sentence-ending punctuation calls for capitals.
guidance.note: Confirms a specific difference from Genius's ad-lib initial-capital convention. This is not permission to lowercase proper nouns or English `I`.

guidance.title: Align the first sound without a lead-in
guidance.statement: Align the first sound without a lead-in; include live speech and remix vocals unless effects make them genuinely indecipherable; listen to the entire track before marking it instrumental.
guidance.note: Authoritative workflow qualification, not proof that current anchors are accurate or that a long opening means an instrumental track.

guidance.title: Supplies brand spellings and context-dependent short names
guidance.statement: Supplies brand spellings and context-dependent short names.
guidance.note: Curated identity evidence; do not expand every nickname or treat brand recognition as certain.

guidance.title: Supplies British, Nigerian, Patois and contemporary slang with meanings and allowed variants
guidance.statement: Supplies British, Nigerian, Patois and contemporary slang with meanings and allowed variants.
guidance.note: These are separate lexical inventories; translating dialect into standard English is not a correction. A token's meaning still matters.

guidance.title: Preserve the dialect actually sung instead of standardizing an original transcription to Bokmål/Nynorsk
guidance.statement: Preserve the dialect actually sung instead of standardizing an original transcription to Bokmål/Nynorsk.
guidance.note: Existing Genius-mode dictionary checks are narrow language curation; never use them to erase sung Norwegian dialect in MXM. Artist origin is suggested human research, not an automatic dialect classifier.

guidance.title: Use normal Norwegian proper-name/acronym case and the company's/product's actual casing
guidance.statement: Use normal Norwegian proper-name/acronym case and the company's/product's actual casing.
guidance.note: Does not expressly revoke the main line-initial rule. Preserve names such as mixed-case brands; do not blanket-case tokens.

guidance.title: Prefer Bokmål for translations into Norwegian
guidance.statement: Prefer Bokmål for translations into Norwegian; compound translations normally join, with hyphens for certain long/readability cases.
guidance.note: The Bokmål preference is translation-specific, not authorization to normalize original dialect lyrics. Compound analysis needs language context.

guidance.title: Sámi is a separate language whose writing must be retained
guidance.statement: Sámi is a separate language whose writing must be retained; knowledgeable transcription is needed. Lyricless joik is described as instrumental.
guidance.note: Do not map Sámi into Norwegian or remove vocables by heuristic. The joik reference to `#INSTRUMENTAL` needs reconciliation with the main interior-only marker rule and track-level instrumental workflow.

guidance.title: English nouns embedded in German use noun capitals
guidance.statement: English nouns embedded in German use noun capitals; English clauses retain English grammar; borrowed verbs/adjectives remain lowercase; specified adjective+noun combinations capitalize both.
guidance.note: Token-level “English-looking word” detection cannot choose the rule. Existing Genius title-case diagnostics are not a German grammar engine.

guidance.title: A curated elision table depends on actual sung pronunciation and explicitly allows alternatives in several entries, including apostrophized/non-apostrophized forms
guidance.statement: A curated elision table depends on actual sung pronunciation and explicitly allows alternatives in several entries, including apostrophized/non-apostrophized forms.
guidance.note: Encode allowed sets and scope, not a single canonical rewrite. Absence from a supplemental table cannot prohibit an official allowed form.

guidance.title: Audible producer tags are lyrics
guidance.statement: Audible producer tags are lyrics; a recognition list is supplied.
guidance.note: Broad agreement on preserving vocals. A list of known tags never authorizes insertion of an unheard tag.

guidance.title: Dialect-shortened words can be independent words without elision apostrophes
guidance.statement: Dialect-shortened words can be independent words without elision apostrophes; contractions of separate words use apostrophes.
guidance.note: Do not “repair” every shortened German dialect token as omitted Standard German letters.

guidance.title: Terminal punctuation is limited to necessary question/exclamation marks and closing parentheses/quotes. Hyphens mark incomplete words
guidance.statement: Terminal punctuation is limited to necessary question/exclamation marks and closing parentheses/quotes. Hyphens mark incomplete words; ellipses mark incomplete sentences, not ordinary performance pauses.
guidance.note: Review interruption/phrase context; do not strip closing syntax or infer ellipses from pauses.

guidance.title: A shortened single word generally omits the apostrophe unless it distinguishes another real word
guidance.statement: A shortened single word generally omits the apostrophe unless it distinguishes another real word; merged-word contractions use an apostrophe; established colloquial abbreviations can be exceptions.
guidance.note: Genius's general omission-apostrophe guidance cannot be applied as an unconditional Spanish MXM rule.

guidance.title: Normal accents remain
guidance.statement: Normal accents remain; an apostrophe does not replace an accent. Retain original `s`/`z` if aspiration/substitution is audible, omitting only when entirely absent.
guidance.note: Accent checks can be scoped; phonetic presence requires listening.

guidance.title: Actual direct speech uses colon + space + opening quote + capital. Omit the colon if it would end a line. Quotation may span lines. Indirect speech has no colon/quotes
guidance.statement: Actual direct speech uses colon + space + opening quote + capital. Omit the colon if it would end a line. Quotation may span lines. Indirect speech has no colon/quotes; hypothetical quoted words keep quotes but receive no colon or automatic initial capital.
guidance.note: Explicit conflict with `MX-F13`'s comma. Review and encode the Spanish exception; do not apply a global quote-prefix transform.

guidance.title: Lead normally opens the line and determines sync
guidance.statement: Lead normally opens the line and determines sync; sequential secondary lyrics are plain, overlapping/background lyrics parenthesized. Unison/harmony is written once; echoes/reverb/nonhuman effects are excluded. In live performances, a lead's audience-directed aside takes parentheses unless alone on its line. Audience vocals are plain when carrying lyrics or standing alone, otherwise follow background treatment.
guidance.note: Role/overlap/effect classification needs audio or supplied facts. Performer identity alone does not decide role; text similarity does not prove an echo or simultaneous unison.

guidance.title: Put secondary text midline only where a lead pause accommodates it, otherwise favor line end. Avoid initial parentheses
guidance.statement: Put secondary text midline only where a lead pause accommodates it, otherwise favor line end. Avoid initial parentheses; remove them when they enclose an entire line. No punctuation immediately before an opening parenthesis.
guidance.note: Structural edits can change timing and vocal attachment; require role/placement evidence. No unconditional “move all parentheses” conversion.

guidance.title: Normally lowercase openings, with grammatical/name and sentence-ending-punctuation exceptions
guidance.statement: Normally lowercase openings, with grammatical/name and sentence-ending-punctuation exceptions.
guidance.note: Confirmed conflict with Genius's capital-initial ad-lib convention; grammar remains a precondition.

guidance.title: Acronyms use uppercase without separating dots/spaces
guidance.statement: Acronyms use uppercase without separating dots/spaces; laughter units use commas.
guidance.note: Do not infer acronym or laughter role from arbitrary letters.

guidance.title: Context can justify words above ten
guidance.statement: Context can justify words above ten; the source illustrates a large quantity without a complete exception predicate.
guidance.note: The generic >10 conversion is not unconditional. Review fixed/contextual expressions and large values.

guidance.title: Preserve artist/band spelling/case
guidance.statement: Preserve artist/band spelling/case; detailed grammar distinguishes names, religion, geography, celestial objects, titles, dates and ordinary nouns. Mentioned artist, song and album names may be quoted.
guidance.note: No generic proper-name normalization. Direct speech is not the only permitted quotation role. The current Genius Spanish dictionary rules cover only a small subset.

guidance.title: Contains contextual homophone distinctions and explicit accent conventions, including unaccented `solo` and specified demonstratives/short verb forms
guidance.statement: Contains contextual homophone distinctions and explicit accent conventions, including unaccented `solo` and specified demonstratives/short verb forms.
guidance.note: Record source-specific lexical cases; not a general accent-removal operation. Meaning-dependent pairs remain review.

guidance.title: At most 70 characters per lyric line and ten lines per stanza
guidance.statement: At most 70 characters per lyric line and ten lines per stanza.
guidance.note: Adds a limit missing from the main plan. Unicode counting unit and stanza/tag relationship are unspecified; review the count definition before enforcement and never auto-split at character 70.

guidance.title: Commas follow grammatical lists/appositions/vocatives, not every audible pause
guidance.statement: Commas follow grammatical lists/appositions/vocatives, not every audible pause; coordination has specific exceptions.
guidance.note: Grammar/audio timing are different inputs; no pause-based comma insertion.

guidance.title: Exclamation marks, colons and semicolons are prohibited, with an exception for punctuation belonging to a sung song title
guidance.statement: Exclamation marks, colons and semicolons are prohibited, with an exception for punctuation belonging to a sung song title.
guidance.note: Conflicts with general MXM allowance and Genius's excitement-based exclamation convention. Scope the reviewed French rule and name exception explicitly.

guidance.title: Required question marks have no preceding space, for grammatical questions or clearly questioning delivery
guidance.statement: Required question marks have no preceding space, for grammatical questions or clearly questioning delivery.
guidance.note: Specific typography rule, not a blanket import of ordinary French publishing spacing. Delivery still needs judgment.

guidance.title: Mark beginning/end elisions with apostrophes
guidance.statement: Mark beginning/end elisions with apostrophes; retain standard spelling for internal elisions.
guidance.note: Do not share an unconstrained Genius/English apostrophe inserter.

guidance.title: Join imperatives and pronouns with hyphens
guidance.statement: Join imperatives and pronouns with hyphens; verlan retains underlying spelling and hyphenates rearranged syllables.
guidance.note: Needs grammatical/lexical interpretation; no arbitrary syllable splitting.

guidance.title: The prose spells sub-ten or “precise” times, but its examples also use numeric times with minutes. Exactly ten is not specified
guidance.statement: The prose spells sub-ten or “precise” times, but its examples also use numeric times with minutes. Exactly ten is not specified.
guidance.note: Internally ambiguous source: retain wording and block automatic boundary decisions until clarified.

guidance.title: `y a` has no apostrophe
guidance.statement: `y a` has no apostrophe; French decade expressions and embedded English decade expressions have different constructions.
guidance.note: Explicit language scope, including mixed-language spans; no global decade-apostrophe rewrite.

guidance.title: Above-ten quantities normally use digits, but fixed expressions stay in words
guidance.statement: Above-ten quantities normally use digits, but fixed expressions stay in words.
guidance.note: Numeric interpretation must exclude fixed expressions; no blanket >10 conversion.

guidance.title: Avoid disruptive midphrase backing/echo placement
guidance.statement: Avoid disruptive midphrase backing/echo placement; significant backing material can appear at line end or separately.
guidance.note: Does not provide a reliable text-only echo-deletion predicate. Preserve until role/placement is established.

guidance.title: Use original Japanese script even when release metadata is romanized
guidance.statement: Use original Japanese script even when release metadata is romanized; do not add furigana/readings, including unusual readings. Artist-selected kanji matter; use Japanese glyph forms rather than Chinese variants.
guidance.note: Header-English policy on Genius is unrelated. Distinguish pronunciation glosses from actual backing vocals before any removal; no global Han-character normalization.

guidance.title: Structure belongs in tagging. Explicit A-melody/pre-chorus/chorus labels have stated mappings
guidance.statement: Structure belongs in tagging. Explicit A-melody/pre-chorus/chorus labels have stated mappings; B-melody, solo and C-melody labels each allow more than one target. Intro/outro refer to sung sections, not pure instrumental edges.
guidance.note: Some explicit source labels support mapping; ambiguous labels require choice. Preserve source labels and musical identity.

guidance.title: Halfwidth spacing/commas can aid phrasing and readability
guidance.statement: Halfwidth spacing/commas can aid phrasing and readability; line breaks follow meaning and singability.
guidance.note: No automatic spacing at every script boundary or split at a fixed character count.

guidance.title: Vocalization spelling and Katakana/Latin choice depend on pronunciation, ordinary usage and official lyrics
guidance.statement: Vocalization spelling and Katakana/Latin choice depend on pronunciation, ordinary usage and official lyrics; repeated vocables can use hyphens/spaces/line breaks by phrasing.
guidance.note: No universal romanization/interjection replacement or separator.

guidance.title: Separate blocks with blank lines, but says a blank is not needed immediately after `#INSTRUMENTAL`
guidance.statement: Separate blocks with blank lines, but says a blank is not needed immediately after `#INSTRUMENTAL`.
guidance.note: Directly conflicts with `MX-S12` requiring that blank. Do not silently select an automatic spacing policy.

guidance.title: Lists Latin line starts, proper nouns/acronyms and parenthetical beginnings among capitalization cases
guidance.statement: Lists Latin line starts, proper nouns/acronyms and parenthetical beginnings among capitalization cases; rejects arbitrary all-caps/all-lowercase/title-case presentation.
guidance.note: Parenthetical wording differs from main grammatical-only guidance; exact mixed-script/parenthetical scope needs resolution.

guidance.title: Children's lyric kanji/kana choices depend on intended age
guidance.statement: Children's lyric kanji/kana choices depend on intended age.
guidance.note: Audience metadata/human judgment; no universal all-kana conversion.

guidance.title: Avoid excessive Japanese corner quotes in dialogue
guidance.statement: Avoid excessive Japanese corner quotes in dialogue; line breaks/halfwidth spaces/parentheses can support long spoken content.
guidance.note: General comma-plus-quotes treatment is not a universal Japanese conversion.

guidance.title: Use fullwidth question/exclamation marks after fullwidth preceding characters, ASCII forms after halfwidth characters
guidance.statement: Use fullwidth question/exclamation marks after fullwidth preceding characters, ASCII forms after halfwidth characters.
guidance.note: Define and review width classification for mixed scripts and punctuation; no NFKC normalization of the whole draft.

guidance.title: Where strict sentence alignment fails, meaning may be redistributed over its existing two or three lines while total line count stays fixed
guidance.statement: Where strict sentence alignment fails, meaning may be redistributed over its existing two or three lines while total line count stays fixed.
guidance.note: Qualifies the main translation instruction. Preserve translation alignment; linguistic translation remains outside the transformer.

guidance.title: Native-script lyrics and romanized forms in the Translation surface are distinct. Editing automatic romanizations is restricted to high-rank Curators. The current article gives no usable complete per-language romanization list
guidance.statement: Native-script lyrics and romanized forms in the Translation surface are distinct. Editing automatic romanizations is restricted to high-rank Curators. The current article gives no usable complete per-language romanization list.
guidance.note: Preserve content kind and script. Do not claim that Arabic/Korean automatic romanization is available from this page title.

guidance.title: Lyrics, Sync, Tag and Translate are separate tabs
guidance.statement: Lyrics, Sync, Tag and Translate are separate tabs; Tag contains structure and performer work. Some contributions can be locked; Credits has a different Pro scope.
guidance.note: Confirms separate metadata workflow, not clipboard/interchange support or access for every user.

guidance.title: Translation must be personally authored, not copied or machine-translated, with context and original untranslatable terms preserved
guidance.statement: Translation must be personally authored, not copied or machine-translated, with context and original untranslatable terms preserved.
guidance.note: Document scope; the deterministic format engine does not translate lyrics.

guidance.title: Music-only tracks have a track-level instrumental flag. English FAQ also describes marking a whole track instrumental after full listening
guidance.statement: Music-only tracks have a track-level instrumental flag. English FAQ also describes marking a whole track instrumental after full listening.
guidance.note: Whole-track status is documented; exact community submission controls/text payload remain unverified. Do not emit interior-marker syntax as the entire track.

guidance.title: Publisher/label partner workflows support CSV/JSONL/DDEX and dedicated synced-lyric delivery
guidance.statement: Publisher/label partner workflows support CSV/JSONL/DDEX and dedicated synced-lyric delivery; text preserves breaks/paragraphs. The inspected JSONL schema has no structure/performer-range fields.
guidance.note: Official import formats exist, but they do not establish an available ordinary-community import for our retained metadata.

guidance.title: Community-built, explicitly nonbinding, dated January 28, 2025. Adds punctuation/name/time exceptions, date-ordinal spelling, regional English, sung letters, melisma and separator advice
guidance.statement: Community-built, explicitly nonbinding, dated January 28, 2025. Adds punctuation/name/time exceptions, date-ordinal spelling, regional English, sung letters, melisma and separator advice.
guidance.note: Do not elevate every recommendation to official MXM policy. Date ordinals can conflict with a broad reading of the main numeric-date rule; semantic/audio evidence still matters.

guidance.title: Linked contributor teaching guide
guidance.statement: Linked contributor teaching guide; no visible date. Recommends musical/meaningful boundaries and states a 70-character limit.
guidance.note: This is weaker general-language evidence than the official Spanish FAQ's explicit limit. Unicode count and stanza/tag cardinality remain unspecified.

guidance.title: Dated July 7, 2026
guidance.statement: Dated July 7, 2026; explicitly says some advice differs from official requirements. Prefers `whoa`, colon before direct speech, standalone hyphen for full censoring, round-number exceptions, sung-`Uhr` time rules, and further punctuation/voice conventions.
guidance.note: `whoa` conflicts with Genius's `woah`; comma→colon conflicts with main MXM. Preserve advisory standing and context. Omission of an apostrophized alternative from its table does not prohibit one allowed by official German Insights.

policyNotes: Use only this Musixmatch corpus. Official Musixmatch source standing is independent of Genius staff/editorial authority; community supplements remain advisory.

Every clause records its language scope, handling and remaining limits. A syntactic check is not full verification. Unresolved source conflicts, audio evidence, numeric meaning and unknown words never justify a guessed edit.
Switching is a deterministic, lossless local representation operation. The assistant never runs conversion and must not reinterpret switching as permission to edit lyrics.
No complete Arabic or Korean language-specific policy has been established by the inspected sources. Do not claim that generic checks or an English fallback fill this gap.

Main-page finite slang forms: ballin', 'cause (because), cuz (cousin), 'em, gon' or gonna, I'ma, outta, 'til, yo (greeting), yo' (possessive). Meaning is a precondition; there is no unconditional replacement of every matching spelling.
